summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests adding bevacizumab to atezolizumab and chemotherapy (carboplatin and etoposide) in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer that has spread to the liver. Study drugs are given by IV every 3 weeks: 4 induction cycles of atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin and etoposide, then maintenance with atezolizumab and bevacizumab for up to 12 months or until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The study measures how long the cancer does not get worse (progression-free survival) and whether the treatment is safe and tolerable.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa agregar bevacizumab a atezolizumab y quimioterapia (carboplatino y etopósido) en cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas en estadio extensivo que se ha diseminado al hígado. Los medicamentos se administran por vía intravenosa cada 3 semanas: 4 ciclos de inducción con atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatino y etopósido, seguidos de mantenimiento con atezolizumab y bevacizumab por hasta 12 meses o hasta progresión o toxicidad inaceptable. El estudio mide cuánto tiempo el cáncer no empeora (supervivencia libre de progresión) y si el tratamiento es seguro y tolerable.
who_for: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with radiographic liver metastases at diagnosis.
Small cell lung cancer confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
No prior treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
Measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1.
not_for: Deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism or other significant blood clot in the 3 months before first dose.
Blood pressure not controlled (systolic above 150 or diastolic above 100 mmHg).
Tumor invading or abutting major blood vessels.
Active or past autoimmune disease or immune deficiency, except the listed exceptions.
